$comment: Shared cases for the OOBE update interval (backend TimeAttributionCalculator) and its live label (web lib/osUpdateLive.ts). See README.md.

scenarios.name: long_update_three_restarts
scenarios.description: Field shape e4ecd6f8: the page starts after the ESP exit, CBS stages and installs the LCU, three restarts with the package mid-servicing, then a confirmation visit; the desktop follows 92 s after it, before the wait would show.

scenarios.name: wait_for_sign_in_with_standby
scenarios.description: Update before AccountSetup, two restarts, then 48 minutes at the lock screen, 45 of them in standby: the wait shows 2 minutes after the package reached Installed, the AccountSetup declaration does not end it, the Hello wizard does.

scenarios.name: cancelled_page
scenarios.description: AllowOOBEUpdates=0: the page cancels within seconds and the restart page passes through. No update, no hint.

scenarios.name: update_without_restart
scenarios.description: The page installs without a restart and stops with success: nobody was signed out, so the hint ends with the stop. The names_capped marker after the stop is a page record and moves the end, as in the time attribution.

scenarios.name: late_agent_first_run
scenarios.description: Field shape 6a7d241d: the session started at T0, the agent's first run at 26:30, after the page start. The servicing steps it backfills arrive with it; the first page name begins the update, and once a package it serviced shows up again the begin moves back to that package's first step (20:00). The package the OOBE finished at 5-7 min stays out.

scenarios.name: failed_download
scenarios.description: Field shape e7551b82: only the servicing stack is staged, the download fails after 25 minutes, the page restarts the device and the second visit offers nothing. The outcome reads failed, the staged KB not installed; the device waits for its user.

scenarios.name: failure_then_skip
scenarios.description: Field shape cb1992b8: visit 1 fails and restarts the device; visit 2 downloads again and someone selects Skip. The new download after the restart reads as running, not as waiting.

scenarios.name: names_without_servicing
scenarios.description: Update names without a page start and without servicing steps: the first name begins the update; the stop ends it without a restart, so the hint ends with it.

scenarios.name: missed_first_visit
scenarios.description: The agent saw visit 1 only by its names (no page start, no ESP exit) and the confirmation visit after the restart: the first name begins the update until the package shows up again, then the package's first step does.

scenarios.name: whiteglove_part_two
scenarios.description: Pre-provisioned device, update in the user part two days later: the window starts at the resume, the part-1 ESP never bounds it.

scenarios.name: rows_before_window_start
scenarios.description: The agent's first run at 10:00 reads back update page rows from 5-6 min, before the session started: they lie outside the window, and a page start inside it without evidence of its own begins nothing until its visit holds some.

scenarios.name: restart_reported_late
scenarios.description: After the restart the servicing step reaches the backend before the agent reports the restart: the update reads as restarting until the report, then as finished. lastBootUtc carries no zone (UTC, as the backend reads it); the page start carries a 7-digit fraction.

scenarios.name: names_after_user_back
scenarios.description: Update names after the Hello wizard: that update runs beside the enrollment, not instead of it. No interval, no hint.

scenarios.name: failed_declaration
scenarios.description: The enrollment declares Failed while the update runs: the update's time ends there, a servicing step after it is not the update's, and the hint goes away.

scenarios.name: failed_without_restart
scenarios.description: The download fails and the page stops with fail; the restart page passes through without a restart and the package stays mid-servicing. The update gave up, so the open package does not keep it running: it ended, until the user is back.

scenarios.name: page_fails_while_package_awaits_restart
scenarios.description: Field shape 26b98b13 / f49084c2: the LCU reached reboot_required, then the page timed out and stopped with fail before its restart. Windows still finished the LCU across two restarts. A package waiting for its restart keeps the update running whatever the page reported; the wait begins after the confirmation visit.
